name: MCP destructive-action guardrails -- the SAFETY layer above PREMCP's AUTH layer ("so they dont accidentally delete the whole onedrive")
description: Andrew-direct (2026-06-26, verbatim 'so they dont accidentally delete the whole onedrive'). CTO-authored PRD docs/architecture/SCTY_MCPGUARD_PRD.md (commit 0019b1743), parallel to SCTY_PREMCP. The SAFETY layer that sits ABOVE PREMCP's AUTH layer: PREMCP governs WHO can call the gateway; MCPGUARD governs WHAT a destructive call can do once authorized. KEY FRAMING (CTO): contain-don't-classify -- ONE guard mitigates BOTH the honest fat-finger AND the hijacked-agent injection, because both end at the same destructive Graph call (no intent-classification needed -- that's a separate workstream's burden). Load-bearing context: the m365 MCP gateway is now the SINGLE MS-Graph chokepoint (Andrew-sovereign 2026-06-26: NFRA_MSGRAPH consumes Graph THROUGH the gateway, no new registration) -- so the guardrails sit at ONE chokepoint, which is the elegant place to enforce them. SIX guardrails: G1 BLAST-RADIUS CAP (the OneDrive-stopper -- a single call cannot touch more than N items / a whole tree), G2 classification gate (read vs write vs destructive), G3 confirm-on-destructive (human/second-factor confirm before a destructive call lands), G4 reversibility-first/undo (DENY permanent-delete, route to recycle bin -- recoverable by default), G5 rate-limit / anomaly detection, G6 audit / alert (every destructive call logged + alertable). Aligned to NFRA_MSGRAPH S6 (multi-user) + the delegated-token-via-gateway model (the same chokepoint NFRA_MSGRAPH S2 uses).
